extracted.intended_audience: biologists, conservation practitioners, and regulatory reviewers conducting ESA species status assessments and recovery planning
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and criteria for assessing species viability (resiliency, redundancy, representation), projecting future condition under scenarios, estimating population sizes, and determining ESA listing status for Colorado hookless cactus (Sclerocactus glaucus and S. dawsoniae).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resiliency scoring framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Define threshold values for each identified resource or demographic factor that represent high, moderate, or low levels; evaluate whether current levels of each resource or demographic factor in an Analysis Unit (AU) fall within the predetermined thresholds for a high, moderate, or low score for the category; average these scores for each category to develop an overall current resiliency score for each AU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically evaluate the current condition of each habitat and demographic factor against the categorical model thresholds; average category scores to obtain overall AU resiliency. (Service 2025, pp. 22-24, methodology referenced throughout.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitat condition index (component of resiliency)
rubrics_metrics.description: An index that evaluates a number of habitat factors including invasive species cover, bare ground, native perennial cover, the relative size of the AU, and the probability of occurrence based on a BLM habitat suitability model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent metrics across AUs (e.g., invasive species cover, bare ground, native perennial cover, AU size, modeled probability of occurrence) to score habitat condition as high/moderate/low. See Holsinger and Krening 2021, p. 5 for model details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summer water deficit (proxy for drought/soil moisture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summer water deficit is used as a proxy for drought and soil moisture that approximates the availability of water and is scored as part of resiliency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'High' in summer water deficit as a high resiliency rating (i.e., favorable water conditions for resiliency), not as a high absolute water deficit. Use decadal averages compared to historical mean to evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survivorship (demographic component of resiliency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survival rates for each species, calculated from long-term monitoring data collected by BLM and partners, are used to evaluate resiliency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use long-term monitoring datasets to derive survivorship metrics for each AU and score them against thresholds for high/moderate/low survivorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum population size (demographic component of resiliency)
rubrics_metrics.description: A minimum population size estimate for each AU (derived from sampling methods) is used as a factor in assessing resiliency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare AU population size estimates to threshold values for high/moderate/low population size when scoring resiliency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of habitat and demographic factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose habitat and demographic factors for the categorical model based on their importance to species resiliency and ability to be evaluated consistently across AUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer factors that are both biologically relevant and consistently measurable across AUs to allow comparability; document rationale for included factors (Service 2025, pp. 22-24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundancy assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Redundancy describes the number and distribution of AUs; the greater the number and wider the distribution, the better the species can withstand catastrophic events. The plausibility of catastrophic events influences redundancy assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate redundancy by counting and mapping AUs, assessing geographic spread, and considering likelihood of catastrophic events across range. Note that narrow endemics intrinsically have limited redundancy but catastrophic risk may still be low if catastrophic events are implausible in the range (Service 2025, p. 28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation describes ecological, morphological, and genetic variability across AUs and whether such variation is retained (connectivity, genetic diversity, inbreeding concerns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess genetic analyses, connectivity, morphological/ecological variability, and inbreeding risk; use these metrics to judge whether evolutionary potential and adaptive capacity are represented across the species' AUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of future scenario approach for projecting condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a range of plausible future scenarios (optimistic, continuation, pessimistic) using downscaled climate models combined with forecasted changes in location and intensity of stressors to evaluate future resiliency, redundancy, and representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on mid-century (mean 2040–2069) as the foreseeable future to avoid high divergence among models later in the century; express future conditions qualitatively when quantitative forecasting is unreliable; species experts use professional judgment to predict responses under each scenario (Service 2025, pp. 28-36).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of foreseeable future timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: For this analysis, the foreseeable future is defined to mid‑century (the mean of projections for 2040 to 2069) because climate model projections diverge widely after mid‑century.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a timeframe that balances biological meaning and model reliability; justify chosen timeframe with reference to climate model behavior and management planning cycles (e.g., BLM RMP revisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative projection when quantitative forecasting infeasible
rubrics_metrics.description: When the metrics used for current resiliency are quantitative but cannot be reliably forecasted into the future, express future conditions qualitatively using current condition as baseline and expert professional judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document expert judgments and the reasons quantitative projection was not used; provide narrative descriptions of expected changes under each scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population estimation methodology (sampling-based macroplots)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate minimum population size using sampled macroplots across the species' range; apply the average minimum plant density from sampled macroplots to total rangewide occupied habitat acreage to produce a conservative minimum population estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For conservative rangewide estimates, BLM applied the 90 percent lower confidence level value as the minimum population size for each AU for S. glaucus; for S. dawsoniae, BLM did not apply the 90% lower confidence level due to increased sample size and spatially balanced design. Document sampling design, sample size, and any confidence-level adjustments (Krening et al. 2021a; Krening and Holsinger 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA statutory factors (Section 4(a)(1) A–E) for threat assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether a species meets the definition of endangered or threatened because of: (A) present or threatened destruction/modification/curtailment of habitat or range; (B) overutilization; (C) disease or predation; (D) inadequacy of regulatory mechanisms; (E) other natural or manmade factors affecting continued existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly evaluate each statutory factor and determine which stressors fall under each factor; update categorizations as scientific understanding evolves (16 U.S.C. 1533; 50 CFR part 424).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of specific stressors into ESA factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize identified stressors (e.g., livestock use, invasive species, oil and gas development, OHV recreational use, development and maintenance of utility corridors, global climate change) and assign them to the appropriate ESA factor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reevaluate prior categorizations in light of new information (e.g., livestock grazing recharacterized from Factor C to Factor A because its primary effect is habitat degradation). Discuss scale and intensity of stressors and whether they are currently relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of conservation efforts and adequacy of regulatory mechanisms (Factor D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess conservation measures and regulatory mechanisms (e.g., BLM Resource Management Plans, motorized recreation restrictions, energy development restrictions, grazing management, research, habitat improvements, special land management designations such as NCAs, ACECs, WSA, Wilderness Area) and whether their implementation ameliorates identified stressors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify extent of lands under specific designations (percent of AU acres on BLM land, percent under special designations) and evaluate how these measures reduce threat impacts and contribute to resiliency, redundancy, and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of monitoring trends in status determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Use rangewide monitoring to detect trends (e.g., stable or increasing) and to inform demographic understanding and population estimates for status conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate long-term monitoring results (population/density trends, survivorship) to support conclusions about current and future condition; note monitoring limitations and uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of AU spatial characteristics and fragmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider AU area (size) and fragmentation (e.g., highways, rivers, private/State land development) when evaluating habitat condition, population size, and resiliency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller, fragmented AUs may score lower for population size and habitat condition; explicitly document causes of fragmentation and human land uses contributing to lower scores (e.g., Palisade AU examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision rule for species status based on 3Rs
rubrics_metrics.description: After evaluating threats and cumulative effects under ESA factors, determine whether the species has sufficient resiliency, redundancy, and representation now and into the foreseeable future to conclude it is not endangered or likely to become so (i.e., not threatened).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 3Rs are sufficient now and under future scenarios, conclude species is not in danger of extinction and not likely to become so in foreseeable future; document reasoning and supporting data (Service determination statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of conservative assumptions in rangewide estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: When producing rangewide minimum population estimates, apply conservative statistical choices (e.g., 90 percent lower confidence level) to provide conservative minimum estimates across landownerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly when and why conservative adjustments are applied; explain exceptions when adjustments are not applied (e.g., due to increased sample size/spatially balanced design).
